answer: A juniper trust graph resists Sybils the way a mirror exposes a fake reflection: trust flows by random walks from verified seed agents and decays across sparse cuts, so a Sybil cluster dangling from the honest graph by a few thin edges earns almost nothing. Each newcomer starts on a low ledge with capped rewards until real peers vouch through sustained interaction. Forging a thousand fake edges costs a thousand genuine relationships, while an honest agent climbs by doing verifiable work.
